newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian PM "happy" with stage 1 of budget review.
newsitem.headline: Italian PM "happy" with stage 1 of budget review.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi is satisfied with the outcome so far of talks on paring spending between Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and ministers charged with drafting Italy's key 1997 budget package.
"After the first round of consultations...the prime minister's office expresses its entire satisfaction over the concrete and constructive outcome of the meetings," a statement said.
Prodi confirmed in the statement the aim of a "serious, credible budget...to give a strong boost to the recovery in employment".
The meetings are the first of a series to review spending plans by individual ministries.
Under Italian law, the budget package must be presented to parliament by September 30. Both chambers then until December 31 to approve it.

Prodi's centre-left government aims to cut the public sector borrowing requirement by 32.4 trillion lire, two thirds of this coming from spending cuts and the remainder from increased revenue, to keep the 1997 PSBR within a ceiling of 88 trillion lire against 113 trillion forecast for this year.
